thread:
Anna: Quick heads-up — ran profiling on dedicated4 (A100x4) comparing prefill vs decode for mixed-quant models (FP8 + INT8 + 4bit fallback). Posting highlights.
Raj: nice. TL;DR?
Anna: Prefill shows higher TPS on the FP8 path, but TTFT spikes on long contexts (>16k) because KV cache eviction + kernel selection swaps happen during prefill. Decode path keeps TTFT more stable — we pick decode-optimized kernels earlier.
Mike: do you have traces/logs?
Anna: pasted flamegraph link in thread, but summary: prefill spends ~60% time in copy+dequant kernels and ~20% in attention kernel-switch overhead. Decode spends ~45% in matmuls with less dequant noise.
perf-bot: [auto] profiling summary: prefill_deq_hotpath=0.62, kv_evictions_per_sec=3.4 @ seq_len>8192, kernel_switches_per_req=1.7
Liz: sounds like our kernel selection gating is triggering too late during prefill. If kernel switch happens mid-prefill we pay expensive copies and KV layout reorgs.
Raj: proposal: make batching/scheduler aware of "expected total tokens" so for long-prefill requests we bias towards kernels that keep KV layout stable even if slightly slower per-op.
Mike: did calibration affect the runtime choices?
Anna: yes — INT8 calibration reduced compute cost but harmed output quality for some prompts. FP8 calibration caused the runtime to pick FP8 kernels that don't support fused-KV layout -> extra dequant + copy step.
Anna: example config used for the run:
```json
{"kernel_policy":"seq-aware","kv_eviction_threshold":0.75,"fallback_order":["fp8","int8","4bit"],"batcher":{"prefer_decode_for_short":true}}
```
Liz: Can we A/B gate a seq-length heuristic: if avg_prefill_len_last_min > X, force "kv-stable" kernel family? Cheap to compute and avoids mid-request swaps.
Raj: Also consider decode-priority for short response-length routes so we don't hurt TTFT for tail-latency sensitive callers.
Mike: I'll spin a canary with kv_eviction_threshold lowered and seq-aware kernel gating. Will run 1k mixed-length requests.
perf-bot: canary results uploaded: prefill TPS down 10% but TTFT p95 improved 22% on longctx (>16k). KV evictions dropped from 3.4/s to 0.6/s.
Anna: good win. Next steps: make kernel selection sticky for prefill+decode when safe, add seq-aware gating to batcher heuristics, and add a regression alert if kernel_switches_per_req increases > 0.2 vs baseline.
Liz: filing follow-ups: perf playbook entry + small runtime PR for the gating logic. I'll assign Mike to the canary dashboard and Raj to the alert.
Mike: ack, will post dashboard links when ready.
Raj: thanks — let's keep an eye on quality deltas after INT8/FP8 calibration changes. Ping me if the A/B shows >5% quality regression.
Anna: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
